worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)={3}^{x/2}$ and the given matrix $K,$ we have

$$
{3}^{K/2}={3}^{\frac{1}{2}PJ{P}^{-1}}=P\cdot ({3}^{J/2})\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $J$ is a Jordan block with $4$s on the main diagonal, we have

$$
f(J)=[\begin{aligned}f(4) & {f}^{′}(4) \\ 0 & f(4)\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative of $f$ is ${f}^{′}(x)=\frac{{3}^{x/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{2}.$ So, we get

$$
{3}^{J/2}=[\begin{aligned}f(4) & {f}^{′}(4) \\ 0 & f(4)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & \frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{2} \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1\cdot 1-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{K/2} & =P\cdot ({3}^{J/2})\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & \frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{2} \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18-9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & 9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-9 \\ -18 & 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9-9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & 9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ -9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & 9+9\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Given a function f and matrices A and S, where S is invertible, we have f(SAS−1)=S⋅f(A)⋅S−1.

For f(x)=3x/2 and the given matrix K, we have

3K/2=312PJP−1=P⋅(3J/2)⋅P−1.

Now, since J is a Jordan block with 4s on the main diagonal, we have

f(J)=[f(4)f′(4)0f(4)].

The derivative of f is f′(x)=3x/2ln⁡(3)2. So, we get

3J/2=[f(4)f′(4)0f(4)]=[99ln⁡(3)209].

Also, the inverse of P is

P−1=11⋅1−12⋅1[1−12−11]=[2−1−22].

Therefore, we conclude that

3K/2=P⋅(3J/2)⋅P−1=[11211][99ln⁡(3)209][2−1−22]=[11211][18−9ln⁡(3)9ln⁡(3)−9−1818]=[9−9ln⁡(3)9ln⁡(3)−9ln⁡(3)9+9ln⁡(3)].
